 7

 8                           UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
                           NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA
 9                              SAN FRANCISCO DIVISION
10
      Join Digital, Inc.                                   Case No. _____________
11
              Plaintiff.
12

13    Pivium, Inc.                                         COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES

14            Defendant.                                   JURY TRIAL DEMANDED

15
            Plaintiff Join Digital, Inc. (“Join Digital”) alleges as follows:
16
                                              I. Summary of Action
17
            Join Digital and Defendant Pivium, Inc. (“Pivium”) entered into a contract that required
18

19   Pivium to install state of the art office audio visual systems in eleven business offices in San

20   Francisco earmarked for use by a Join Digital customer. Pivium, however, turned in a problem-
21   plagued performance and substantially missed the completion date, requiring major remedial
22
     clean up to fix the mess Pivium left. In addition, as the project began its deep decline, rather than
23
     rise to the occasion, Pivium wrongfully interfered with the Join Digital customer. The defective
24
     contractual performance and wrongful behavior inflicted substantial financial harm on Join
25

26   Digital and damaged its customer relationship, and reduced the prospects for additional business

27   with other building tenants.
                                                       1
28
                                         JOIN DIGITAL COMPLAINT
               Case 3:24-cv-09138        Document 1         Filed 12/17/24     Page 2 of 8


 1                                                  II. Parties

 2      1. Join Digital is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business in California.
 3
        2. Join Digital develops and sells networking software and associated hardware delivered as
 4
     a cloud service to medium sized and large enterprises, as well as owners of commercial office
 5
     buildings.
 6
        3. Pivium is an Arizona corporation with its principal place of business in Phoenix, Arizona.
 7

 8      4. Pivium holds itself out to the general public as a nationwide full-service design and

 9   integration company that provides integrating technology, content, and modern audio-visual
10   products for work spaces. Pivium touts their design audio visual solutions as enhancing the
11
     human experience by working “tirelessly with facility owners, designers and project staff to
12
     ensure” that their work meets “the needs of the project no matter the space.” Pivium claims that
13
     “it is the design and not the technology” that is the essential factor in the ultimate experience of a
14

15   space.

16                                        III. Jurisdiction and Venue

17      5. The amount in controversy in this matter exceeds $75,000 and thus the Court has subject
18   matter jurisdiction pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1332.
19
        6. Venue in this Court is proper pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(2).
20
                                          IV. General Allegations
21
        7. In March 2023, based on Pivium’s written proposal, Join Digital and Pivium entered into a
22

23   written contract for the provision of extensive audio-visual design product services (the

24   “Contract”), which is attached as Exhibit 1.

25      8. The Contract included a scope of work detailed in a series of promises and warranties that
26
     Pivium made regarding display, provision, and installation of audio-visual functional
27
                                                       2
28
                                         JOIN DIGITAL COMPLAINT
              Case 3:24-cv-09138         Document 1          Filed 12/17/24   Page 3 of 8


 1   components for eleven office spaces for a Join Digital customer: a boardroom, a medium

 2   conference room, and nine small conference and huddle rooms at 655 Montgomery Street, San
 3
     Francisco (the “Project”).
 4
        9. Pivium also promised at the conclusion of the Project to provide an as-built system
 5
     documentation and a control system, windowing configuration and DSP control code, as well as
 6
     equipment MAC addresses for IP address assignment and DHCP reservations working with the
 7

 8   IT coordinator of the Join Digital customer.

 9      10. As part of the Project, Pivium promised to conduct preventive maintenance during
10   standard business hours scheduled thirty days in advance that included, among other things, a
11
     “thorough inspection” of each system the contract covered, resolution of any issues the
12
     inspection identified, and a “thorough cleaning” of system components.
13
        11. Pivium agreed to provide extensive maintenance services “upon substantial completion
14

15   [of the Project]” for a period of thirty-six months.

16      12. The Project completion date was August 1, 2023, which would allow Join Digital to train

17   its client in the use of the technology on August 7, 2023. Pivium understood that Join Digital and
18   its customer were relying on Pivium to timely deliver what it promised. Pivium represented it
19
     was “committed to providing a first class project completion.”
20
        13. The Project eventually devolved into a disaster. Among others, the Project suffered these
21
     problems:
22

23          a. Pivium improperly installed and delivered several defective hardware items.

24          b. Pivium failed to set display resolution on screens correctly, creating an unprofessional
            and unacceptable appearance.
25
            c. Pivium improperly installed power and electrical systems.
26

27          d. Pivium failed to provide manuals for hardware needed for customer training.
                                                       3
28
                                        JOIN DIGITAL COMPLAINT
              Case 3:24-cv-09138         Document 1         Filed 12/17/24   Page 4 of 8


 1
            e. Pivium left spare and uninstalled parts and trash scattered about as an emblem of its
 2          unprofessionalism.
 3
            f. Pivium installed and charged Join Digital for unnecessary, superfluous equipment.
 4
            g. Pivium’s lack of skills and incompetence led to numerous technology errors, including
 5          frozen screens and poor resolution and poor functionality.
 6          h. Pivium incorrectly installed microphones in the boardroom space.
 7
            i. Pivium’s work was riddled with poor, unprofessional quality.
 8
            j. Pivium’s communication throughout the Project deployment was choppy, inconsistent,
 9          and unclear, exacerbating the sundry performance issues.
10          k. Pivium went around the back of Join Digital and contacted its customer directly to
11          interfere with its relationship and complain about the lack invoice payment from Join
            Digital as Join Digital was trying to salvage the mess Pivium had created and respond to
12          customers complaints regarding Pivium’s poor performance.

13          l. Pivium sold Join Digital superfluous equipment to inflate its revenue, which required
            that Join Digital spend time and money to de-install the equipment.
14

15          m. Pivium failed to cure the many problems it created.

16          n. Pivium missed the Project deadline of August 1, 2023.

17          o. Pivium did not provide the promised maintenance services.
18      14. An example that is representative of Pivium’s shoddy work product is its installation of
19
     microphones in the customer’s boardroom, an all-important space for customer operations.
20
     Rather than install the microphones in accordance with manufacturer specifications and
21
     instructions (and sheer common sense), Pivium took it upon itself to install the microphones at a
22

23   location in the boardroom—well behind the conference table where people sit—where the

24   microphones could not function effectively. This ineptness required Join Digital to retain another

25   vendor to relocate the microphones—above the conference table—where voices during meetings
26
     can reach the entire room effectively, at substantial cost.
27
                                                       4
28
                                        JOIN DIGITAL COMPLAINT
              Case 3:24-cv-09138          Document 1       Filed 12/17/24     Page 5 of 8


 1      15. Two months after the Project deadline, Pivium still had not finished what it had

 2   promised, requiring Join Digital to devote significant hours to complete the Project and train its
 3
     customer, which created a substantial delay in delivering functional spaces to the customer. To
 4
     make matters worse, over the following year, additional problems arose with Pivium’s work
 5
     product that required retention of a new vendor to fix them.
 6
        16. Pivium effectively abandoned the Project in October 2023 before it was even functional,
 7

 8   despite its promise to provide three-years of post-project services in the Contract.

 9      17. Join Digital relied on Pivium’s purported expertise that their design and product
10   selections were state of the art and would result in the best possible customer experience for Join
11
     Digital’s customer.
12
        18. Pivium’s unprofessional performance and wrongful conduct compromised the
13
     development and expansion of Join Digital’s relationship with its end user customer and
14

15   undermined new commercial opportunities with other tenants.

16                                         First Claim for Relief
                                           (Breach of Contract)
17
        19. Join Digital incorporates by reference each of the preceding allegations as though fully
18
     set forth in this paragraph.
19
        20. As alleged in the preceding paragraphs, including paragraphs 13 and 14, Pivium
20
     materially breached the Contract.
21
        21. Join Digital has performed all its obligations under the Contract with Pivium except those
22
     for which performance was by law excused.
23
        22. Because of Pivium’s various breaches of contract, Join Digital had to perform substantial
24
     remedial work, including retaining a replacement vendor to complete the Project, to redo
25
     Pivium’s failed work product, a direct and proximate result of which Join Digital suffered
26
     monetary damages in excess of the jurisdictional limit.
27
                                                      5
28
                                         JOIN DIGITAL COMPLAINT
              Case 3:24-cv-09138         Document 1         Filed 12/17/24     Page 6 of 8


 1                                      Second Claim for Relief
                        (Breach of the Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing)
 2
         23. Join Digital incorporates by reference each of the allegations in paragraphs 1 through 18
 3
     as though fully set forth in this paragraph.
 4
         24. By virtue of California law, the Contract included an implied covenant of good faith and
 5
     fair dealing.
 6
         25. Join Digital has performed all its obligations under the Contract with Pivium except those
 7
     for which performance was by law excused.
 8
         26. Pivium’s unprofessional and wrongful conduct in communicating with the Join Digital
 9
     customer unfairly interfered with the benefits under the Contract for Join Digital and breached
10
     the covenant of good faith and fair dealing.
11
         27. As a proximate result of Pivium’s conduct, Join Digital has suffered financial injury in an
12

13   amount to be established at trial but in excess of the jurisdictional requirement.

14                                         Third Claim for Relief
                                       (Breach of Express Warranty)
15
         28. Join Digital incorporates the allegations of paragraphs 1 through 18 as though full set
16

17   forth in this paragraph.

18       29. Pivium is in the business of providing the type of audio-visual technology design it
19   promised to provide in the Contract and holds itself out as possessing special knowledge and
20
     skill in that market niche.
21
         30. Pivium knew that the design product it warranted under the Contract was not only
22
     integral to the agreement of the parties but also was earmarked for use by a specified Join Digital
23

24   customer in several suites of workspace at 655 Montgomery Street in San Francisco.

25       31. Pivium knew that Join Digital, in entering into the Contract, intended to, and Join Digital

26   did, rely upon the special knowledge and skills that Pivium claimed to possess.
27
                                                       6
28
                                         JOIN DIGITAL COMPLAINT
              Case 3:24-cv-09138          Document 1        Filed 12/17/24     Page 7 of 8


 1      32. The design product that Pivium provided did not perform as Pivium warranted,

 2   constituting a breach of express warranty.
 3
        33. Join Digital took reasonable steps to notify Pivium of the problems with its design
 4
     product, which Pivium in response failed to correct or remedy.
 5
        34. The failures of the Pivium design were a substantial factor in causing financial injury to
 6
     Join Digital.
 7

 8                                        Fourth Claim for Relief
                                       (Breach of Implied Warranty)
 9
        35. Join Digital incorporates the allegations of paragraphs 1 through 18of this complaint as
10

11   though full set forth in this paragraph.

12      36. Pivium knew that the design product it promised to provide under the Contract was not

13   only integral to the agreement of the parties but also was earmarked for use by a specified Join
14   Digital customer in several suites of workspace at 655 Montgomery Street in San Francisco.
15
        37. Among other claims, Pivium claims to possess “years of engineering experience to help
16
     (customers) design and install effective content distribution systems that work” and “the
17
     knowledge and experience required to design and build highly reliable video systems that can
18

19   receive content from a variety of sources and deliver it in a variety of ways as the situation

20   demands.”

21      38. Pivium knew that Join Digital, in entering into the Contract, intended to rely upon the
22
     special knowledge and skills that Pivium claimed to possess.
23
        39. Join Digital justifiably relied on the promised skill and judgment of Pivium in entering
24
     into the Contract.
25
        40. The design product Pivium sold Join Digital was not fit for the purpose for which Join
26

27   Digital intended, constituting a breach of implied warranty.
                                                       7
28
                                         JOIN DIGITAL COMPLAINT
              Case 3:24-cv-09138          Document 1        Filed 12/17/24     Page 8 of 8


 1       41. Join Digital took reasonable steps to notify Pivium of the problems with its design

 2   product, which Pivium in response failed to correct or remedy.
 3
         42. The unsuitability of the Pivium design product was a substantial factor in causing
 4
     financial injury to Join Digital.
 5
                                              Prayer for Relief
 6
             Join Digital requests the following remedy awards:
 7

 8           1. Economic damages according to proof;

 9           2. Incidental damages according to proof;
10           3. Consequential damages according to proof;
11
             4. Costs and expense.
12
                                         Demand for Trial By Jury
13
             Join Digital demands that its claims be tried to a jury.
14
      Dated December 17, 2024
15                                                    FINESTONE HAYES LLP
16

17                                                    /s/ Stephen D. Finestone
                                                      By: Stephen D. Finestone
18                                                    Attorneys for Plaintiff Join Digital, Inc.
